subtasks.title: activity infrastructure: countingWriter + Linux procfs group read-counter poller
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: provider_subsystem.md §2 — internal/provider/procgroup_unix.go (!windows build tag) already does Setpgid so PGID==PID is kernel-guaranteed; procgroup_windows.go is the platform-split precedent to mirror with //go:build linux / //go:build !linux files. external_procfs_notes.md — pgrp is FIELD 5 of /proc/[pid]/stat; comm (field 2) may contain spaces/parens so the robust parse splits after the LAST ')'; a reaped pid's stat open fails ENOENT (tolerate as member-gone, never alias); rchar (/proc/<pid>/io) counts bytes returned by SUCCESSFUL read-family calls (pipes/tty/sockets count, pagecache hits count, failed reads count nothing); a reaped child's ioac folds into its parent's rchar (inflates group sums — safe direction, can only false-positive activity within the group, never false-negative); /proc/<pid>/io is readable for same-uid dumpable processes (PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS), no root; a full /proc sweep over ~1100 pids costs ~13ms (~2.6% duty at 2Hz).
2. INPUT: none — new files (internal/provider/activity.go, activity_linux.go, activity_other.go); leaf subtask.
3. LOGIC: Implement FR-A3's two channels as standalone primitives, NO Execute changes here: (a) activity.go — countingWriter: wraps a bytes.Buffer behind a mutex, satisfies io.Writer, records an atomic last-write monotonic timestamp on every Write; exposes LastWrite() time.Time and a Bytes() snapshot (buffer growth during Wait is the activity signal — no data races); (b) activity_linux.go — groupReadBytes(pgid int) (uint64, bool): scan /proc/[0-9]*/stat, parse each stat after the LAST ')' to read pgrp (field 5), filter pgrp == pgid, sum members' /proc/<pid>/io rchar; per-member ENOENT tolerated; returns (_, false) when /proc is unavailable; (c) activity_other.go (!linux) — stub returning (_, false) so non-Linux builds compile and report 'no channel'. Tests ride: poller against the test's own process group (spawn a child that reads a known number of bytes; assert the counter moves; ENOENT race tolerated); countingWriter concurrency test under go test -race; GOOS-gated build check for the stub.
4. OUTPUT: provider.countingWriter + provider.groupReadBytes — consumed by P1.M2.T1.S2 (the Execute idle watcher).
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change (internal primitives).

3. LOGIC: (a) signature → Execute(ctx, spec CmdSpec, dl Deadlines, vb *ui.Verbose) — hard cap keeps the existing WithTimeout shadow (dl.Hard; Hard <= 0 ⇒ unbounded as today when timeout==0 if that is current behavior); stdout/stderr become countingWriter instances (FR-A3(a) pipe channel, always recorded); (b) idle watcher goroutine per D3/D4: armed iff dl.Idle > 0 AND (runtime.GOOS == "linux" OR spec.ProgressiveStdout); ~0.5s tick; single idle clock reset by whichever channel moved last (max of pipe last-write timestamp, poller last rchar-change); on expiry it triggers the SAME group-kill as the hard cap (cancel via a dedicated context.WithCancel wrapping the same cmd.Cancel path) and records the idle cause; the watcher observes ctx.Done() (hard cap / parent cancel / interrupt) and exits; (c) define here the CmdSpec.ProgressiveStdout bool field (Render sets it in P2.M1.T1.S1; it stays false until then ⇒ non-Linux + print-mode = idle disarmed = exactly v3.4 behavior); (d) idle kill returns an ErrIdleDeadline sentinel whose Is() method satisfies errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) (D2/FR-A5) so EVERY existing branch works unchanged; hard cap keeps returning context.DeadlineExceeded; (e) new ui.VerboseCause(reason) helper (internal/ui) emitting 'DEBUG: cause: idle deadline (60s without observable activity)' / 'DEBUG: cause: hard cap (600s)', invoked by Execute on either deadline kill (D6); extend the Execute doc comment: error contract now 'idle OR hard cap ⇒ errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)'; (f) internal/cmd/models.go:150 call site passes Deadlines{Idle: 0, Hard: <existing cfg.Timeout bound>} with a comment (not a role call — idle unarmed). Mock: none — stub shell scripts per the existing executor_test.go harness. Tests ride: hard-cap test updated to the new signature; NEW — silent stub killed at tiny idle (Linux, or any platform with ProgressiveStdout forced true in the test spec); healthy-slow stub emitting a byte every ~0.5s for ~3× idle NOT killed (ProgressiveStdout forced true — portable pipe-activity proof); Linux-only build-tagged test: stdout-silent stdin-reader stub kept alive past idle by the read counter.
4. OUTPUT: the new Execute contract + ui.VerboseCause + CmdSpec.ProgressiveStdout — consumed by P1.M2.T1.S3 (call sites) and P2.M1.T1.S1/S2 (event mode).

RESEARCH NOTE: provider_subsystem.md §6 — internal/provider/parse.go is a 5-step pipeline; empty output yields ok==false (no error); the StderrHint empty-output CAUSE mechanism lives in executor.go:23–38 (this is the path FR-S3 feeds); all five native event modes are NDJSON-ish (FR-S1) with the verified naming trap: claude/cursor/agy offer BOTH json (single buffered object) and stream-json (progressive) — only stream-json qualifies; pi --mode json, codex --json, opencode --format json are the progressive ones.

LOGIC: (a) when spec.ProgressiveStdout: parse stdout as a sequence of JSON events; a per-provider Extractor (registered against the manifest Name) identifies the TERMINAL MESSAGE EVENT and returns the assembled final message (D8: extraction is code living in Go alongside the built-ins; per-provider terminal-event shapes are recorded at verification time in P2.M2); (b) FR-S3: an error/abort event with no terminal message event surfaces its text through the EXISTING StderrHint empty-output cause path (or a precedence sibling when event mode produced no message) — replacing the opaque empty-stdout parse failure; a failed response does NOT reliably produce a nonzero exit (pi documents this) so detection must key on the event stream, not the exit code; (c) print-mode path completely untouched. Tests ride: fake JSONL stub emitting progressive events + a terminal message → assembled message AND not idle-killed under a tiny idle (the portable pipe-activity payoff of FR-A3 — runs on every platform); error-event stream → cause surfaced, empty message handled by the existing parse-retry path; unregistered-extractor guard from S1.
4. OUTPUT: the complete event-mode execution path; consumed by P2.M2.T1.S1 (verification harness) and P2.M2.T1.S2–S5 (extractor registration + population).

subtasks.title: codex (--json) verification + heartbeat judgment
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: FR-S2's recorded pitfall — codex emits a steady ~27-byte stderr heartbeat every ~2s (a timer: liveness, NOT progress) plus periodic ~1.1MB local file re-reads that bump the read counter; per §9.30 the read-counter channel remains the honest signal even in event mode. The spec's own framing is a hypothesis to CONFIRM empirically, not assume.
2. INPUT: verification protocol from P2.M2.T1.S1; installed codex CLI (else ship [] + record).
3. LOGIC: dated empirical verification of 'codex --json' (JSONL events): is emission progressive beyond the heartbeat during real generation? Record the terminal-event shape and error surfacing. JUDGMENT to record with the date: event_stream may still qualify IF emission is otherwise progressive (and FR-S3 error surfacing may justify it) — the heartbeat means the idle clock alone is not proof of progress here, which the HARD CAP bounds (FR-A2); if emission is heartbeat-only, ship [] with that finding. Mock: none (empirical).
4. OUTPUT: codex manifest disposition with the heartbeat judgment recorded.
5. DOCS: Mode A — dated header comment in the codex builtin manifest.
